pagerbot: :rotating_light: P0 alert - tp4 collective rendezvous hang detected on gpufleet-14 (ranks timing out). Auto-pager sent to #incidents. thread_ts=4598760001
Devon (oncall): I'm on it. seeing a spike in `ncclAllReduce` latencies, most jobs stuck in `rendezvous.wait()`; starting triage.
Maya (sre): Noted. Any obvious OOM or CUDA Xid in dmesg?
Devon (oncall): quick grep of pod logs shows repeated: `NCCL WARN Call to cudaMemcpy timed out` then `ncclCommAbort: NCCL_COMM_ABORTED` and some `cuda: an illegal memory access was detected (Xid 79)`. Full snippet:
```
Rank 3: NCCL WARN AllReduce timeout after 120s
Rank 3: ncclCommAbort on communicator 0x7f3c...
E CudaDrv: an illegal memory access was detected (Xid 79)
container: exit 137
```
Devon (oncall): Ranks 0-7 still alive, ranks 8-15 show container crashes. Looks like a partitioned set of ranks.
Ariana (infra): I'm seeing transient IB flaps on node-03 and node-07 in gpufleet-14 around the same time (loss of link for ~22s). NIC counters show packet drops and link resets.
Liam (ml-runtime): That fits a multipartition: tensor-parallel rendezvous expects all TP ranks across nodes; if a subset loses fabric, the rendezvous can hang waiting for peer. We should treat as network partition + some nodes hitting OOM/CUDA faults when retrying recv.
Priya (solutions): Customer impact check: endpoint `/gen/tx-omega` reporting 502/timeout for some requests (observed ~6.8% error rate in last 8 minutes). CS already fielding a few tickets.
Devon (oncall): Immediate mitigation plan: 1) mark affected nodes `cordon` and drain new scheduling 2) route new TP workloads to fallback DP-reshard variant 3) restart crashed containers on the isolated nodes after NIC fixes 4) enable per-route fallback in routing policy to model-variant v1-small in host region.
Maya (sre): I'll take node cordon/drain. Running: `kubectl cordon gpufleet-14-node-03 && kubectl drain gpufleet-14-node-03 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data`
Ariana (infra): I'm rolling NIC firmware reset and reconfiguring the SR-IOV VF bindings on node-03 and node-07. Watching link counters. If link flaps persist we may need to replace the NIC.
Liam (ml-runtime): I'll push a temporary routing rule: route `model:tp4` -> `model:tp4-fallback-dp` for this region and add a 2x timeout backoff. Command: `redwoodctl routes update --endpoint /gen/tx-omega --fallback model:tp4-fallback-dp --timeout 10s`
Devon (oncall): Doing canary: put 10% traffic to fallback first. If stable, increase gradually.
ops-bot: :gear: runbook snippet applied: `TP_PARTITION_WORKAROUND`: set env `REDWOOD_TP_FAILOVER=1` on route and toggle `inference.fallback.enabled=true`.
Priya (solutions): Notifying impacted customers: drafting a quick message stating degraded availability for a small subset of TP endpoints; ETA 30-45m for full recovery, will update.
Maya (sre): Node-07 NIC shows restored link at +00:04, pod restarts happening. Logs from restarted pods show `ncclInitGraph: communicator created` then immediate `AllReduce stuck waiting for peer 12`.
Liam (ml-runtime): That suggests mixed state: some peers restarted and rejoined but their local KV cache/DP sharding offsets mismatched -> collective handshake fails. I'll add jittered restart for remaining pods to avoid thundering herd.
Devon (oncall): Running `for p in $(kubectl get pods -l app=tp4 -o name); do kubectl delete $p --grace-period=0 --force; sleep 4; done` to sequentially restart.
Jordan (SRE Lead): Please record timeline for postmortem. Keep traffic routing logs and kernel dmesg, NIC counters. Also capture `nvidia-smi -q -d MEMORY,UTILIZATION` snapshots from affected nodes.
Ariana (infra): NIC counters show a burst of 18k retransmits around alert time; we had a scheduled maintenance earlier in the day changing fabric MTU on a different rack — correlating that now.
Priya (solutions): Customer update sent: "We're experiencing degraded inference for certain high-parallel endpoints in US-west-2; our mitigation is routing traffic to fallback variants. We'll follow up with a root cause and ETA." :white_check_mark:
Devon (oncall): After sequential restarts, TP jobs are now reestablishing; error rate dropped to ~0.3% over 5m. Canary at 25% looks stable.
Liam (ml-runtime): Observed one lingering job with `cuda kernel launch failed: out of memory` — killed and restarted with reduced batch size. Need to check autoscaling and resource requests for TP pods.
Maya (sre): Recording actions: cordoned node-03/07, sequential pod restarts, applied routing fallback, NIC firmware reset on 2 nodes, canary traffic.
Jordan (SRE Lead): Good work. Next: 1) Postmortem ticket (INC-459876) assigned to Maya + Ariana + Liam; 2) add a permanent route fallback for TP endpoints with `REDWOOD_TP_FAILOVER` enabled; 3) update runbook to include multipartition detection heuristics (split rank counts + NIC retransmits).
Devon (oncall): Will stay on until stable for 2h; handing off to Maya for overnight observation. @Maya please confirm.
Maya (sre): Taking handoff. I have runbook and escalation steps, channel marked with `:lock:` for oncall handover.
Priya (solutions): CS to follow up with affected customers with postmortem once available.
Devon (oncall): Final note: cause looks like transient IB fabric partition + consequent cuda Xid and OOM during retry. Root cause investigation will confirm if MTU change earlier triggered fragmentation.
Ariana (infra): Opening hardware ticket for node NICs; if we see recurrence we'll schedule replacement.
Jordan (SRE Lead): :thumbsup: Once postmortem draft is ready, ping me for review. Closing incident alert but leaving thread open for notes.
ops-bot: Incident INC-459876 created and assigned. Postmortem checklist added. :white_check_mark:
